steps.prompt: Your friend says a film was “good”. What questions would you ask to find out what they really mean?

cards.title: Vague words hide your meaning
cards.body: Good, bad, nice, things and stuff could mean almost anything. Replace them with words that say exactly what you mean: “Exercise is good” → “Exercise strengthens the heart and improves sleep.”

cards.title: Academic verbs
cards.body: Essays use precise verbs to talk about evidence and ideas: demonstrates, suggests, indicates, reveals, affects, influences, improves, reduces. “The study demonstrates…” sounds more exact than “The study says…”.

cards.title: Vague → precise
cards.text:
Vague: Plastic does bad things to the ocean.
Precise: Plastic bags choke sea turtles and break into tiny pieces that fish swallow.
cards.note: Exact nouns and verbs give the reader a picture.

prompts: Which precise word are you proudest of?
Which vague word will you watch for in your final essay?
